title: Univariate multiquadric approximation: reproduction of linear polynomials
contribution: Proves that univariate multiquadric approximations reproduce all linear polynomials when the only condition on the centres is that they are unbounded above and below, via a divided-difference (hat-function) basis, and shows that for c != 0 the span of the multiquadrics is dense in C[a,b] on any finite interval.
problem_entry: Conjecture that polynomial reproduction (known on the integer lattice via Fourier transforms: Jackson 1987, Buhmann 1988) does not need a regular grid, attacked first in d = 1 with arbitrary unbounded centres (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: The naive space S0 of absolutely convergent translate sums contains no polynomials (pp. 4-6), so move to multiquadric hat functions (second divided differences) written through a positive Peano kernel acting on the piecewise-linear interpolant of the coefficients; linear reproduction then follows from kernel moment identities (pp. 3, 7-9).
assumptions: d = 1; centres strictly increasing and unbounded in both directions, no spacing conditions (pp. 3-4); admissibility = absolute convergence for every x (p. 3); c != 0 for the kernel positivity and density results (pp. 7, 11, 13).
proof_devices: characterization lemma reducing 'absolutely convergent for every x' to one summability condition by splitting off the finite index set near x (2.3)-(2.4), (3.11)-(3.12) (pp. 4, 7-8)
B-spline/Peano-kernel representation of second divided differences, psi_j = (1/2) int B_j(theta) phi''(x-theta) dtheta with phi'' > 0 (3.4)-(3.6) (p. 7)
reproduction via kernel moment identities: unit integral (3.13) and vanishing odd moment (3.14) (pp. 8-9)
epsilon-T split of a tail integral (3.22)-(3.24) (p. 10)
far-centre Taylor expansion plus explicit Vandermonde-type solution with bounded products (4.8)-(4.10), then Weierstrass (pp. 11-12)
experiments: none; a practitioner's report (Philip Smith, IMSL: centres diverging in least-squares fits) is explained by Theorem 6 (p. 14)
positioning: Extends Buhmann (1988) by removing uniform spacing when d = 1 (p. 3); builds on Hardy 1971 and Jackson 1987 (p. 2); credits Nira Dyn's private results in detail (p. 14).
writing: States why the conjecture matters before the plan (p. 2); conclusion judges the result against the original aim (p. 13); explicit self-criticism ('Unfortunately', p. 3; 'inelegant', p. 13).
limits_future: Confined to the univariate case (p. 3); S2 construction inelegant and misses important approximants such as lattice cardinal functions that reproduce quadratics (pp. 13-14); future: larger space (5.1), uniqueness, multivariate lines of centres (5.3) whose conditions are stronger than necessary (pp. 13-14).

title: Tabulation of thin plate splines on a very fine two-dimensional grid
contribution: An algorithm and Fortran package that tabulate a thin plate spline on a very fine square grid in O(h^-2 + n eps^(-1/3) |log h|) work instead of O(h^-2 n), by recursive mesh halving with O(h^6) biharmonic-aware stencils and explicit treatment of terms near their centres, with a closed-form analysis of all higher-order truncation terms.
problem_entry: Application posed by Ian Barrodale: thin-plate-spline image warping (medical images, shipping channels, satellite pictures of forests) needs s at up to 10^8 grid points with n ~ 200-500, where direct evaluation is impracticable (pp. 1-4).
key_idea: Each TPS term is smooth away from its centre, so subtabulate by recursive halving with O(h^6) stencils made exact on quadratics and cleared of the fourth-order term by the biharmonic equation; delete and later re-add terms whose centres are within rho*h, with rho = ceil((6/eps)^(1/6)) (pp. 3-11).
assumptions: Distinct, non-collinear interpolation points (p. 3); relative accuracy eps per term, with the log factor ignored on a scale-invariance argument (p. 11); stability of recursive stencil use not analysed (p. 14).
proof_devices: stencil weights from polynomial exactness plus biharmonic identity (2.3)-(2.10) (pp. 5-6)
sixth-derivative bound 72/(x^2+y^2)^2 (3.10) converted into the neighbourhood size rho (pp. 10-11)
scale invariance: change of units adds a quadratic, which the stencils reproduce (p. 11)
closed-form complex derivatives of the TPS kernel and exact t-th order error terms by rotational symmetry (Lemmas 1-5, pp. 17-21), showing higher-order terms add at most 6.2% for rho >= 10 (p. 20)
experiments: Table 1: workstation times for grids 100^2-800^2 and n = 25-400 at eps = 1e-6, split into subtabulation and correction costs (about n/100 s per halving), vs direct evaluation 395.56 s (n = 25) on 800x800; timing noise of at least 1% disclosed (pp. 14-15).
positioning: Adopts TPS warping of Barrodale, Berkley and Skea and Duchon's variational justification (p. 2); relates stability to subdivision (Dyn 1992) (p. 14); contrasts with fast multipole methods for general points (p. 16).
writing: Opens with plain-language applications before any formula (p. 2); cost formula in abstract and introduction (pp. 1, 4); acknowledgements record enjoyment of industrial use (p. 21).
limits_future: Error accumulation over recursive halving not analysed (p. 14); names cheaper 1-D stencils (4.1) and working with s instead of s_h as probably more efficient alternatives (pp. 15-16); grid can be split into pieces for storage (p. 15).

title: DAMTP 1997/NA18
contribution: Duplicate Scholar entry: the text is byte-identical to S165 'Trust region calculations revisited' (DAMTP 1997/NA18, carded as core in c01), which argues for the More-Sorensen trust-region subproblem method and makes it affordable for dense quasi-Newton B via banded orthogonal similarity transforms (O(n^{7/3}) or O(n^{11/5}) per iteration).
problem_entry: Community belief that truncated CG (Steihaug) is preferable because More-Sorensen is too expensive, refuted by a two-variable ill-conditioned example and a cost analysis (pp. 1, 3).
key_idea: Keep the More-Sorensen (1-eps)-optimality guarantee, refine the lambda iteration (Newton plus false position), and make each Cholesky cheap by keeping Omega^T B Omega banded with bandwidth about n^{2/3} under rank-one updates (pp. 7-17, 19-20).
assumptions: Euclidean norm (p. 2); symmetric possibly indefinite B (p. 2); dense B changed by rank-one/two quasi-Newton updates for Section 3 (pp. 12-13).
proof_devices: characterization theorem via Lagrangian and negative-curvature perturbation (pp. 4-5)
failed-Cholesky vector u with u^T(B+lambda I)u <= 0 giving a Rayleigh-quotient lower bound on lambda* (2.11) (p. 7)
exact quadratic identity for the MS termination test (pp. 10-11)
Givens-rotation counting O(n^2/(s+1)) shown first on an explicit n = 10, s = 2 pattern (pp. 14-16)
balancing cost monomials, s ~ n^{3/5}, t ~ n^{4/5} (p. 20)
experiments: One timing table copied from Powell (1997): band vs full, n = 50-800 on a Sun 4, giving c ~ 0.12 and savings from n >= 40 (p. 17).
positioning: Defends More-Sorensen against Steihaug; one-sentence mention of Gould, Rendl-Wolkowicz, Sorensen (p. 3); reports Yuan's conjecture favouring CG for positive definite B (p. 19).
writing: Thesis argued in the abstract (p. 1); Discussion critiques the standard questions of convergence theory (pp. 17-18).
limits_future: Practical importance called debatable (p. 17); advantage shrinks for positive definite B with line searches (p. 19); hoped useful for future optimization software (p. 20).
